subject: SparkBridge usage reconciliation — proposed amnesty + commit top-up
messages:
From: Jenna Ortiz <jenna.ortiz@sparkbridge.io>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected usage spike — Dec/Jan overage

Hi Mina,

Hope you're well. We pulled our month-end numbers and there is a significant overage charge that showed up for Dec '25 and Jan '26. We are seeing ~1.1M inference tokens billed as on-demand beyond our committed capacity; that's roughly $18k of unplanned spend on top of our committed invoice.

I attached the raw usage export (sparkbridge_usage_export_Q4-2025.csv). Can someone help reconcile why the spike wasn't throttled into our commit or why it wasn't flagged earlier? Our procurement team (procure@sparkbridge.io) is already asking for a timeline and any remediation steps.

We'd like to avoid churn here — can Redwood propose a short-term remediation (credit / one-time top-up) and an operational fix to prevent recurrence?

Thanks,
Jenna Ortiz
Director, ML Platform
SparkBridge

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected usage spike — Dec/Jan overage

Hi Jenna — thanks for the export and the heads-up. I'm sorry to see this surprise. I’ve looped in Ben (sales) for commercial remediation and Laura (finance) for the billing side. Rishi will look at the routing/policy side to identify why requests weren’t routed to the committed pool or throttled.

Quick asks while we investigate:
- Ben/Laura: can you pull the invoice detail and draft a proposed credit/settlement cadence we can offer as a one-time remediation?
- Rishi: please review the request routing logs for Dec 15–Jan 31 and flag any fallback events or model variant mismatches.
- Jenna: can you confirm whether the burst traffic was tied to a new internal experiment / rollout? If so, list the pulldown start/end times.

I’ll aim to get a preliminary reconciliation and proposed commercial path by end of day Thu. If that timeline is tight for procurement, propose a 30-min sync tomorrow.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Customer Success — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed goodwill amnesty + capacity top-up option

Hi Jenna — thanks for flagging and thanks Mina for triaging. I dug into the usage and finance numbers and here’s a pragmatic path we can offer to close this quickly without a long dispute: 

Proposal (high-level):
- One-time amnesty: Redwood will credit 50% of the unplanned overage charges for Dec/Jan (credit applied to next invoice).
- Commitment Top-up: SparkBridge purchases a 12-month committed top-up equivalent to the remaining monthly delta (we recommend a 30% uplift to cover expected QA/test bursts). This will be billed as a prepaid credit and applied to future consumption.
- Operational action: Redwood will enable a stricter routing policy for your workspace to prefer committed pools for inference by default and add a burst alerting rule.

Numbers (ballpark based on submitted export):
- Unplanned on-demand cost (Dec+Jan): ~$18,000
- Proposed amnesty credit: $9,000
- Recommended prepaid top-up (12 months): $36,000 (applied as credits; effective cost smoothing across the term)

If SparkBridge agrees in principle, we can send a short amendment + invoice draft and route a DocuSign for signatures. We’re prepared to accept a PO referencing Deal SB-2025-42.

Would you be open to this structure or do you need a smaller upfront commit and a phased top-up? Happy to discuss on a quick call.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

- We can apply the $9,000 credit against the first monthly invoice after the amendment is executed.
- The prepaid top-up ($36,000) will be invoiced as a one-time charge with net-30 payment terms unless SparkBridge requests vendor-specific terms.

I expect minimal paperwork — we can convert this to a short amendment (1 page) that updates committed capacity and records the one-time credit.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Proposed goodwill amnesty + capacity top-up option

Thanks — this looks reasonable and I appreciate the flexible approach. A few asks from procurement:
- Can Redwood shift the prepaid top-up invoice to net-45? Our standard is net-45 for one-time vendor prepayments.
- Instead of a single $36k prepaid, would Redwood accept a 3-month phased purchase: $12k now (PO today), $12k in 60 days, $12k in 120 days? That helps our internal cashflow.
- We’d like the amendment to include an explicit rollback clause if our production burst is attributable to a short-term QA experiment (we have internal tickets that may show this).

If you can accept net-45 and a 3x phased top-up, I can push a PO from procure@sparkbridge.io today for the first tranche and we can get the DocuSign sent for the amendment.

-Jenna

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps so we have a single source of truth:

1) Commercials agreed (in principle)
   - Amnesty: Redwood credit $9,000 (50% of Dec/Jan overage) applied to first invoice after amendment execution.
   - Prepaid top-up: $36,000 total, phased in three tranches of $12,000.
   - Payment terms: Redwood accepts net-45 for the prepaid tranches.

2) Operational controls
   - Rishi will enable stricter routing to committed pool for SparkBridge workspace and add a burst alerting threshold of 10% above expected daily median.
   - Rishi to share a short playbook (3 bullets) to avoid similar incidents during experiments.

3) Paperwork and timelines
   - Laura to send final amendment and invoice package via DocuSign (target: EOD Wed 18 Feb). DocuSign link will reference Deal SB-2025-42.
   - SparkBridge to send PO for first $12k tranche to procure@sparkbridge.io today (Jenna) — PDF of the PO to be attached to the DocuSign envelope.
   - Once first PO received and amendment signed, Redwood will apply the $9,000 credit to the next invoice and activate prepaid credits.
   - Follow-up sync: 30-minute call Thu 19 Feb 10:00 PT to confirm routing changes and complete signatures.

Attachments: proposed_amnesty_terms_SparkBridge_v1.pdf, invoice_draft_SB-0467.xlsx

HubSpot Deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/987654/SB-2025-42
DocuSign (pending): https://docusign.com/redirect/doc/ABC123-sparkbridge-amnesty
